answer: Before this account is trusted, a camera watches the eye's micro-saccades, the tiny jumps no two people share, and matches them against a sealed enrolment vault. A signal photograph fails at once: the check needs a living eye, and at the comet of the scan the pupil must track a moving dot the photo cannot follow. Forging one signature means bribing a vault keeper and faking five years of clinic visits, a job priced above 38,000 silver, while the pigment stamp on the vault record turns black if a second eye claims the same pattern.
